title: AI use surges at Travelers as call centre roles reduce - AI News
content:
## AI 商业策略 服务行业 AI 工作世界

一月中旬，保险公司 Travelers 宣布了一项新协议，为 10,000 名工程师和数据科学家配备 AI 助手。然而，不到两周后，Travelers 的领导层解释说，公司真正的竞争优势在于专业知识，而不仅仅是 AI，并相信这才是推动长期利润增长的关键。

据 Travelers 的首席执行官 Alan Schnitzer 称，公司目前有超过 20,000 名专业人员“定期使用 AI 工具”。他还对公司声称的 Travelers 呼叫中心在 AI 帮助下效率得到提升一事发表了评论，这导致了关于呼叫中心裁员的说法。

### AI 技术与创新驱动增长

Schnitzer 表示，Travelers 的净利润有所增长，这主要得益于公司密集的技术和创新战略。据报道，Travelers 在 2016 年至 2025 年间，其售出的保单总价值平均每年增长近 7%。其基础综合赔付率改善了近八个百分点，降至 83.9。

Schnitzer 解释说，对技术的大量投资与利润改善是同步的。“尽管我们的技术支出有所增加，但基础盈利能力的改善包括费用率改善了 3 个百分点或 10%。在过去十年中，我们培养了创新技能组合的竞争优势。现在，我们正将所有这些第一部分的知识带到 Travelers 的创新 2.0 中，由 AI 驱动——并且离量子计算也不远了。”

创新 1.0 关系到公司取得这一成功的战略和基础，公司计划进入一个更先进的阶段，称之为创新 2.0，其中 AI 是核心驱动力。

### 自动化等于呼叫中心裁员

Schnitzer 指出，自动化如何直接减少了人员需求并提高了理赔效率，这在最近的数字中清晰可见。例如，Schnitzer 表示，Travelers 的“理赔呼叫中心人员减少了三分之一”，并且正在采取措施将四个理赔呼叫中心合并为两个。

这种效率提升减少了理赔费用，改善了公司的赔付率。最终，对自动化和分析的投资帮助 Travelers“优化了赔偿支出并提高了运营效率”。

Schnitzer 表示，现在向 Travelers 提出的所有理赔中，超过 50% 有资格进行直通式处理，客户在大约三分之二的情况下采用了这种处理方式。他接着说：“另外 15% 的理赔使用先进的数字工具处理。所有这些百分比都在增长。”

Schnitzer 宣布了这个语音代理的成功，他说：“早期客户的采用率超出了我们的预期。”

### AI 和自动化重塑 Travelers 的运营

据 Schnitzer 称，AI 和自动化的好处是深远的，不仅仅局限于理赔呼叫中心。“其他用例提高了承保决策的质量和效率，并改善了客户、代理人、经纪人和员工的体验。”

Travelers 的执行副总裁兼商业保险总裁 Greg Toczydlowski 谈到了生成式 AI 代理如何被用来“高效挖掘”内部和外部的数据源。这些帮助公司“更好地理解和综合风险特征。” Toczydlowski 补充说，最近增加的代理提高了承保流程的速度并改善了细分定价。

他解释了公司的商业承保人如何表现非常出色，这得益于用于评估风险的先进工具。这些工具包括优化定价和总结过去理赔数据的模型，从而简化了整个流程。

“他们不仅在当今市场上表现出色，而且还帮助塑造了我们行业的转型，” Toczydlowski 说。

Travelers 的执行副总裁兼个人保险总裁 Michael Klein 强调了 AI 在个人保险中的重要性，称其用于使续保承保“更有效、更高效”。

Klein 说：“我们从一个专有的 AI 驱动的预测模型开始，该模型对财产组合中的每个账户进行评分。基于这个分数，最有可能发生损失风险的账户会提交给承保人审查。然后，我们的续保承保平台使用生成式 AI 将数据整合成相关可操作信息的摘要，供我们的承保人评估。”

因此，Klein 表示，平均处理时间减少了 30%。因此，“最终结果是，我们的承保人将精力集中在最有可能提高盈利能力的决策上，并且效率更高。”

在特种保险方面，Travelers 的债券与特种保险总裁 Jeffrey Klenk 评论了 AI 如何将提交接收时间从“几小时缩短到仅仅几分钟”。他还表示，最近已实施 AI 来简化续保流程。

### 创新 2.0 – AI 对工作的影响

尽管理赔呼叫中心的人员已经减少，Schnitzer 并未推测进一步的裁员。相反，他强调了 AI 给 Travelers 带来的日益提高的生产力。“我想说的是，得益于一些生产力和效率举措，人均产出上升了，我们预计人均产出将继续上升。”

据 Schnitzer 称，Travelers 的创新 1.0 战略是公司过去十年强劲利润的关键驱动力。在过去十年中，我们培养了创新技能组合的竞争优势。现在，我们正将所有这些第一部分的知识带到 Travelers 的创新 2.0 中，由 AI 驱动——并且离量子计算也不远了。”

他相信 AI 将使整个财产/意外险领域受益，并强调了最近的先进 AI 工具如何能够“理解和执行复杂的利益相关者互动、定义明确的流程、数据密集型工作流以及海量的非结构化数据。”

Schnitzer 表示，人类专业知识与 AI 结合“放大了现有优势”，并说 Travelers 正在大力投资“AI 和其他复杂的技术解决方案”。他说“数十个规模化生成式 AI 工具已经投入生产。数百万笔交易现已自动化……而且代理式 AI 不是未来的愿景。它已经嵌入到我们今天的业务运营中。”

AI 和自动化技术有望使保险行业发生十倍变革，因为 Travelers 预计此类技术将“以更快、更具成本效益的方式交付新能力”。

从产品开发到新业务拓展，再到承保速度和质量、代理和客户服务等等，AI 正在使 Travelers、其客户和分销合作伙伴受益，展示了该技术在商业和行业中的广泛影响。

## [AI Business Strategy](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/ai-business-strategy/)  [Service Industry AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/service-industry-ai/)  [World of Work](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-and-us/world-of-work/)
Mid-January saw insurance company, [Travelers](https://www.travelers.com/), announce a new deal that empowers 10,000 engineers and data scientists with AI assistants. However, less than two weeks on, Travelers’ leadership explained that the company’s true competitive advantage lies in expertise, not AIs alone, believing this is what will drive longer-term profit growth.
According to Travelers’ chief executive officer Alan Schnitzer, over 20,000 professionals at the company currently “use AI tools regularly.” He also commented on company claims that Travelers’ call centres are experiencing a boost in efficiency at the hands of AI, leading to claims call centre cuts.
### AI technology and innovation driving growth
Travelers’ net profit has increased, according to Schnitzer, largely fuelled by the company’s intensive technology and innovation strategy. Travelers reportedly increased its total value of insurance policies it sold by nearly 7% a year on average between 2016 and 2025. Its underlying combined ratio improved by almost eight points, falling to 83.9.
Schnitzer explained that heavy investment in technology has coincided with improved profits. “Notwithstanding a increase in our technology spending, that improvement in underlying profitability includes a 3-point or 10% improvement in our expense ratio. Over the decade, we developed the competitive advantage of an innovation skill set. Now we’re bringing all that Part 1 know-how to Innovation 2.0 at Travelers, powered by AI – and not too far off quantum computing.”
Innovation 1.0 relates to the company’s strategy and foundation to this success, and it has plans to move into a more advanced stage it’s calling Innovation 2.0, in which AI is the central driver.
### Automation equals call centre culls
Schnitzer noted how automation has directly reduced staffing needs and improved claims efficiency, something clearly seen in recent numbers. For instance, Schnitzer said that Travelers’ “claim call centre population is down by a third,” and steps are being taken to consolidate four claims call centres into two.
Such efficiency gains have reduced loss adjustment expenses, improving the company’s loss ratio. Ultimately, investment in automation and analytics have helped Travelers “refine indemnity payouts and drive operational efficiencies.”
Schnitzer stated that over 50% of all claims made to Travelers are now eligible for straight-through processing, and customers are adopting this processing approximately in two-thirds of cases. He went on to say that: “Another 15% of all claims are processed with advanced digital tools. All of those percentages are growing.”
Schnitzer heralded the success of this voice agent, saying: “Early customer adoption is exceeding our expectation.”
### AI and automation reshaping operations in Travelers
The benefits of AI and automation are far-reaching, beyond just claims call centres, according to Schnitzer. “Other use cases enhance underwriting decision quality and efficiency and improve the experience for customers, agents, brokers and employees.”
Greg Toczydlowski, executive vice president and president of business insurance for Travelers, spoke about how gen AI agents have been used to “efficiently mine” data sources, both internally and externally. These help the company “better understand and synthesise the risk characteristics.” Toczydlowski added that the recent agent additions have boosted the speed of underwriting processes and improved segmented pricing.
He explained how the company’s commercial underwriters are performing very well, enhanced by advanced tools used to evaluate risks. Tools include models that refine pricing and summarise past claims data, streamlining the entire process.
“They’re not only executing with excellence in the market today, but they’re also helping to shape the transformation of our industry,” Toczydlowski said.
Michael Klein, executive vice president and president of personal insurance for Travelers, underscored AI’s importance in personal insurance, saying it is used to make renewal underwriting “more effective and efficient.”
Klein said, “we start with a proprietary AI-enabled predictive model that scores every account in the property portfolio. Based on this score, accounts with the highest probable risk of loss are presented to underwriters for review. From there, our renewal underwriting platform uses generative AI to consolidate data into summaries of relevant actionable information for our underwriters to evaluate.”
As a result, Klein said that there has been a 30% reduction in average handle times. Therefore, “the net result is that our underwriters focus their efforts on decisions most likely to improve profitability and do so more efficiently.”
In Speciality insurance, Jeffrey Klenk, president of bond & speciality insurance at Travelers, commented on how AI has cut times to intake submissions from “hours to just minutes.” He also said AI has recently been implemented to streamline renewals.
### Innovation 2.0 – AI’s impact on jobs
Despite claims call centre headcounts already reduced, Schnitzer did not speculate on further cuts. Instead, he emphasised the increasing productivity AI has brought to Travelers. “What I would say is that per employee is up, thanks to some productivity and efficiency initiatives, and we expect per employee to continue to go up.”
Travelers’ Innovation 1.0 strategy has been the key driver to the company’s strong 10-year profits, according to Schnitzer. Over the decade, we developed the competitive advantage of an innovation skill set. Now we’re bringing all that Part 1 know-how to Innovation 2.0 at Travelers, powered by AI – and not too far off quantum computing.”
He believes that AI is set to benefit the entire P/C landscape, highlighting how recent advanced AI tools are able to “understand and execute the complex stakeholder interactions, well-defined processes, data-intensive workflows and massive amounts of unstructured data.”
Schnitzer said human expertise with AI “amplifies existing strength,” and said Travelers is investing heavily in “AI and other sophisticated technology solutions.” He said “Dozens of scaled generative AI tools are already in production. Millions of transactions are now automated… And agentic AI isn’t a future aspiration. It’s embedded in our business operations today.”
AI and automated technologies are poised to transform the insurance industry tenfold, as Travelers expects such technologies to “result in faster and more cost-effective delivery of new abilities.”
From product development to new business prospecting to underwriting speed and quality, agent and customer service and more, AI is benefiting Travelers, its customers, and distribution partners, showcasing the technology’s vast impact in the business and industry.

title: PepsiCo uses AI to rethink how factories are designed and updated
content:
# 百事公司正利用人工智能重新思考工厂的设计与更新方式

2026年1月30日

![百事公司正利用人工智能重新思考工厂的设计与更新方式](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/PepsiCo-is-using-AI-to-rethink-how-factories-are-designed-and-updated-1024x683.jpg)

这种转变体现在百事公司如何利用人工智能和数字孪生技术，在现实世界中进行改动之前，对其制造设施进行建模和调整。该公司并非在聊天界面或办公工具上进行实验，而是将人工智能应用于其核心问题之一：如何以更快的速度、更低的风险和更少的干扰来配置工厂。

数字孪生是物理系统的虚拟模型。在制造业中，它们可以模拟设备布局、物料流和生产速度。当与人工智能结合时，这些模型可以测试数千种在实际生产线上尝试不切实际或成本高昂的场景。

百事公司一直与合作伙伴合作，将人工智能驱动的数字孪生技术应用于其部分制造网络，早期的试点项目侧重于改进设施的设计和随时间调整的方式。

目标并非为了自动化而自动化，而是为了缩短周期时间。团队无需通过物理试验花费数周或数月来验证变更，而是可以虚拟测试配置，更早地发现问题，并在需要更新时更快地行动。

## 从规划瓶颈到运营捷径

在大型消费品公司，工厂变更往往进展缓慢。即使是微小的调整——新的生产线布局、不同的包装流程或设备升级——也可能需要漫长的规划周期、审批和分阶段测试。每一次延误都会对供应链和产品供应产生连锁反应。

数字孪生提供了一种绕过该瓶颈的方法。通过模拟生产环境，团队可以在接触实际设施之前，了解变更可能如何影响吞吐量、安全性或停机时间。

百事公司的早期试点项目在初始站点显示出更快的验证时间和吞吐量改善的迹象，尽管该公司尚未公布详细的指标。比数字更重要的是这种模式：人工智能正被用于压缩实体运营中的决策周期，而不是取代工人或消除人为判断。

这种用例符合一个更广泛的趋势。超越试点项目的企业通常专注于那些定义明确、范围狭窄的问题，在这些问题上，人工智能可以减少现有工作流程中的摩擦。与开放式的知识工作相比，制造业、物流和医疗运营正显示出更强的吸引力。

## 为何百事公司将人工智能视为运营工程，而非办公效率工具

百事公司的方法也突显了大型企业内部论证人工智能项目价值时一个更低调的转变。其价值与运营成果挂钩——节省的时间、更少的干扰、更好的规划——而非关于生产力的一般性主张。

这种区别很重要。许多企业的人工智能努力之所以停滞不前，是因为它们难以将使用情况与可衡量的影响联系起来。工具部署了，但工作流程保持不变。

数字孪生改变了这种动态，因为它们直接嵌入规划和工程流程中。如果一个模拟的变更能将工厂升级时间缩短数周，其效益是显而易见的。如果它降低了停机风险，运营团队可以随着时间的推移对其进行衡量。

这种对流程变革而非工具的专注，反映了其他行业正在发生的情况。例如，在医疗保健领域，根据本周报道的CEO安迪·贾西的[评论](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/amazon-ceo-andy-jassy-introduces-companys-health-ai-calls-it-highly-personalized-agentic-ai-assistant-that-can-/articleshow/127614051.cms)，亚马逊正在其One Medical应用程序中测试一款人工智能助手，该助手利用患者病史来减少重复的录入工作并支持护理互动。该助手嵌入在护理工作流程中，而不是作为独立功能提供。

这两个案例都指向了同一个经验教训：当人工智能融入现有工作方式时，其采用速度会更快，而不是要求团队发明新的习惯。

## 这对其他企业为何重要

百事公司的数字孪生工作不太可能长期保持独特性。食品、化学品和工业品领域的大型制造商都面临着类似的规划限制和成本压力。许多公司已经在使用模拟软件。人工智能为这些模型增加了速度和规模。

更有趣的是，这揭示了企业人工智能采用的下一阶段。

首先，重心正从广泛、通用的工具转向与特定决策相关的聚焦系统。其次，成功与否更少取决于模型质量，而更多取决于数据质量、流程所有权和治理。数字孪生的效用完全取决于为其提供支持的运营数据。

第三，这类人工智能工作往往不引人注目。它不会产生炫目的演示，但可以重塑公司规划资本支出和管理风险的方式。

这也解释了为何许多公司仍持谨慎态度。构建和维护精确的数字孪生需要时间、跨团队协作以及对物理系统的深入了解。回报来自于重复使用，而非一次性的胜利。

## 百事公司的制造人工智能工作是一个值得关注的低调信号

在人工智能报道中，人们很容易关注新模型、智能体或界面。像百事公司这样的故事指向了不同的方向。它们展示了人工智能正被视为基础设施——一种位于日常决策之下，并逐渐改变工作如何在组织内流动的东西。

对于企业领导者来说，关键并非复制技术栈，而是寻找那些因规划延迟、验证周期或运营风险而拖慢业务的地方。这些摩擦点正是人工智能最有可能扎根的地方。

百事公司的数字孪生试点项目表明，工厂车间可能是当今人工智能最实用的试验场之一——并非因为它时髦，而是因为当时间和错误具有明确成本时，其影响更容易被看到。

_(照片由 [NIKHIL](https://unsplash.com/@vinikhill?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) 拍摄)_

# [PepsiCo is using AI to rethink how factories are designed and updated](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/pepsico-is-using-ai-to-rethink-how-factories-are-designed-and-updated/)
January 30, 2026
![PepsiCo is using AI to rethink how factories are designed and updated](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/PepsiCo-is-using-AI-to-rethink-how-factories-are-designed-and-updated-1024x683.jpg)
Share this story:
## [ai](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/ai/)  [digital twins](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/digital-twins/)  [manufacturing](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/manufacturing/)  [supply chain](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/supply-chain/)
Categories:
## [AI Business Strategy](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/ai-business-strategy/)  [Manufacturing & Engineering AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/manufacturing-engineering-ai/)
That shift is visible in how PepsiCo is using AI and digital twins to model and adjust its manufacturing facilities before making changes in the real world. Rather than experimenting with chat interfaces or office tools, the company is applying AI to one of its core problems: how to configure factories faster, with less risk, and fewer disruptions.
Digital twins are virtual models of physical systems. In manufacturing, they can simulate equipment placement, material flow, and production speed. When combined with AI, these models can test thousands of scenarios that would be impractical — or expensive — to try on a live production line.
PepsiCo has been working with partners to apply AI-driven digital twins to parts of its manufacturing network, with early pilots focused on improving how facilities are designed and adjusted over time.
The goal is not automation for its own sake. It is cycle time. Instead of taking weeks or months to validate changes through physical trials, teams can test configurations virtually, identify problems earlier, and move faster when updates are needed.
### From planning bottleneck to operational shortcut
In large consumer goods companies, factory changes tend to move slowly. Even small adjustments — a new line layout, different packaging flow, or equipment upgrade — can require long planning cycles, approvals, and staged testing. Each delay has knock-on effects on supply chains and product availability.
Digital twins offer a way around that bottleneck. By simulating production environments, teams can see how changes might affect throughput, safety, or downtime before touching the actual facility.
PepsiCo’s early pilots showed faster validation times and signs of throughput improvement at initial sites, though the company has not published detailed metrics yet. What matters more than the numbers is the pattern: AI is being used to compress decision cycles in physical operations, not to replace workers or remove human judgment.
This kind of use case fits a broader trend. Enterprises that move beyond pilot projects often focus on narrow, well-defined problems where AI can reduce friction in existing workflows. Manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare operations are showing more traction than open-ended knowledge work.
### Why PepsiCo treats AI as operations engineering, not office productivity
PepsiCo’s approach also highlights a quieter shift in how AI programs are being justified inside large firms. The value is tied to operational outcomes — time saved, fewer disruptions, better planning — rather than general claims about productivity.
That distinction matters. Many enterprise AI efforts stall because they struggle to connect usage with measurable impact. Tools get deployed, but workflows stay the same.
Digital twins change that dynamic because they sit directly inside planning and engineering processes. If a simulated change cuts weeks off a factory upgrade, the benefit is visible. If it reduces downtime risk, operations teams can measure that over time.
This focus on process change, rather than tools, mirrors what is happening in other sectors. In healthcare, for example, Amazon is testing an AI assistant inside its One Medical app that uses patient history to reduce repetitive intake and support care interactions, according to [comments](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/amazon-ceo-andy-jassy-introduces-companys-health-ai-calls-it-highly-personalized-agentic-ai-assistant-that-can-/articleshow/127614051.cms) from CEO Andy Jassy reported this week. The assistant is embedded in the care workflow, not offered as a standalone feature.
Both cases point to the same lesson: AI adoption moves faster when it fits into how work already gets done, instead of asking teams to invent new habits.
### Why this matters for other enterprises
PepsiCo’s digital-twin work is unlikely to be unique for long. Large manufacturers across food, chemicals, and industrial goods face similar planning constraints and cost pressures. Many already use simulation software. AI adds speed and scale to those models.
What is more interesting is what this says about the next phase of enterprise AI adoption.
First, the centre of gravity is shifting away from broad, generic tools toward focused systems tied to specific decisions. Second, success depends less on model quality and more on data quality, process ownership, and governance. A digital twin is only as useful as the operational data feeding it.
Third, this kind of AI work tends to stay out of the spotlight. It does not generate flashy demos, but it can reshape how companies plan capital spending and manage risk.
That also explains why many firms remain cautious. Building and maintaining accurate digital twins takes time, cross-team coordination, and deep knowledge of physical systems. The payoff comes from repeated use, not one-off wins.
### PepsiCo’s manufacturing AI work is a quiet signal worth watching
In AI coverage, it is easy to focus on new models, agents, or interfaces. Stories like PepsiCo’s point in a different direction. They show AI being treated as infrastructure — something that sits underneath daily decisions and gradually changes how work flows through an organisation.
For enterprise leaders, the takeaway is not to copy the technology stack. It is to look for places where planning delays, validation cycles, or operational risk slow the business down. Those friction points are where AI has the best chance of sticking.
PepsiCo’s digital-twin pilots suggest that the factory floor may be one of the most practical testing grounds for AI today — not because it is trendy, but because the impact is easier to see when time and mistakes have a clear cost.

# 中国超大规模企业押注数十亿美元于智能体AI，商业成为新战场

2026年1月30日

![Philip Oroni/Unsplash 拍摄的照片](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/premium_photo-1725985758251-b49c6b581d17-1024x683.jpg)

人工智能行业向智能体AI——即能够自主执行多步骤任务的系统——的转向，在最近几个月主导了技术讨论。

然而，当西方公司专注于基础模型和跨平台互操作性时，中国的科技巨头正竞相通过商业集成来占据主导地位，这种分歧可能会重塑全球企业部署自主系统的方式。

就在上周，阿里巴巴升级了其通义千问聊天机器人，允许在界面内直接完成交易，将AI智能体连接到其生态系统，包括淘宝、支付宝、高德地图和旅行平台飞猪。该集成支持超过400项核心数字任务，允许用户在平台内比较个性化推荐，并在不离开聊天机器人环境的情况下完成支付。

### 超级应用的优势

腾讯总裁刘炽平在2025年5月的公司财报电话会议上表示，AI智能体可能成为微信生态系统的核心组成部分，该生态系统为超过10亿用户提供集成的消息、支付、电子商务和服务。

这一定位反映了中国在智能体AI部署方面的结构性优势：集成的生态系统消除了制约西方竞争对手的碎片化问题。

“AI智能体将成为超级应用演进的基础，其成功取决于在支付、物流和社交参与方面的深度集成，”Forrester副总裁兼首席分析师Charlie Dai告诉《CNBC》。“像阿里巴巴、腾讯和字节跳动这样的中国公司都受益于集成的生态系统、丰富的行为数据以及消费者对超级应用的熟悉度。”

### 智能体AI的企业发展轨迹

随着智能体AI从辅助工具转变为能够执行复杂工作流的自主行动者，商业应用预示着更广泛的企业影响。行业专家预计，多智能体系统将成为今年AI部署的一个决定性趋势，从消费者服务扩展到组织生产。

### 不同的部署策略

中国集成化与西方可扩展性之间的对比方法，反映了市场结构和监管环境的根本差异，这些差异很可能决定竞争定位。

“中国将优先考虑国内集成和在选定区域的扩张，而美国公司则专注于全球可扩展性和治理，”Dai说。

追求智能体商业的美国参与者包括OpenAI、Perplexity和亚马逊，而谷歌则探索将自己定位为商家、消费者和AI智能体之间的“媒人”——这些方法反映了需要互操作性而非闭环集成的碎片化平台环境。

智能体AI在中国消费领域的快速商业化，为全球企业决策者提供了早期信号，表明随着这些能力的成熟，自主系统可能如何重塑客户获取成本、平台经济和竞争壁垒。

_(照片由 [Philip Oroni](https://unsplash.com/@philipsfuture) 拍摄)_

# [China’s hyperscalers bet billions on agentic AI as commerce becomes the new battleground](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/china-hyperscalers-agentic-ai-commerce-battleground/)
January 30, 2026
![Photo by Philip Oroni/Unsplash](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/premium_photo-1725985758251-b49c6b581d17-1024x683.jpg)
Share this story:
## [agentic ai](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/agentic-ai/)  [ai](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/ai/)  [china](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/tag/china/)
Categories:
## [AI Market Trends](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/ai-market-trends/)  [Deep Dives](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/features/deep-dives/)  [Human-AI Relationships](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-and-us/human-ai-relationships/)  [Retail & Logistics AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/retail-logistics-ai/)
The artificial intelligence industry’s pivot toward agentic AI – systems capable of autonomously executing multi-step tasks – has [dominated](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/agent-ai-as-the-intern-in-2026-prediction-by-nexos-ai/) technology discussions in recent months.
But while Western firms focus on foundational models and cross-platform interoperability, China’s technology giants are racing to dominate through [commerce integration](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/how-shopify-bringing-agentic-ai-enterprise-commerce/), a divergence that could reshape how enterprises deploy autonomous systems globally.
Just last week, Alibaba upgraded its Qwen chatbot to let direct transaction completion in the interface, connecting the AI agent in its ecosystem, including Taobao, Alipay, Amap and travel platform Fliggy. The integration supports over 400 core digital tasks, allowing users to compare personalised recommendations in platforms and complete payments without leaving the chatbot environment.
### The super app advantage
Tencent President Martin Lau indicated during the company’s May 2025 earnings call that AI agents could become core components of the WeChat ecosystem, which serves over one billion users with integrated messaging, payments, e-commerce and services.
The positioning reflects China’s structural advantage in agentic AI deployment: integrated ecosystems that eliminate the fragmentation constraining Western competitors.
“AI agents will be foundational to the evolution of super apps, with success depending on deep integration in payments, logistics, and social engagement,” Charlie Dai, VP and principal analyst at Forrester, told _CNBC_. “Chinese firms like Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance all benefit from integrated ecosystems, rich behavioural data, and consumer familiarity with super apps.”
### Agentic AI’s enterprise trajectory
Commercial applications signal broader enterprise implications as agentic AI moves from auxiliary tools to autonomous actors capable of executing complex workflows. Industry experts expect multi-agent systems to emerge as a defining trend in AI deployment this year, extending from consumer services into organisational production.
### Divergent deployment strategies
The contrasting approaches between Chinese integration and Western scalability reflect fundamental differences in market structure and regulatory environments that will likely define competitive positioning.
“China will prioritise domestic integration and expansion in selected regions, while US firms focus on global scalability and governance,” Dai said.
US players pursuing agentic commerce include OpenAI, Perplexity, and Amazon, while Google explores positioning itself as a “matchmaker” between merchants, consumers and AI agents – approaches that reflect fragmented platform environments requiring [interoperability](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/agentic-ai-scaling-requires-new-memory-architecture/) not closed-loop integration.
The rapid commercialisation of agentic AI in China’s consumer sector provides enterprise decision-makers globally with early signals of how autonomous systems may reshape customer acquisition costs, platform economics and competitive moats as these abilities mature.
